title: MACBOOK M1
subtitle: Evaluation of the MacBook M1
description: What are the capabilities of a MacBook Pro M1?
content: 🔧 Key Technical Specifications (Base M1)
• 8-core CPU (4 high-performance + 4 efficiency cores)
• 7 or 8-core integrated GPU (depending on the model)
• 16-core Neural Engine for AI tasks and machine learning
• Unified memory of 8 GB or 16 GB (shared RAM + VRAM)
• Ultra-fast SSD (from 256 GB to 2 TB or more)
• Battery life: up to 20 hours
• Passive cooling system (Air) or active cooling system (Pro)
⚡️ Performance
• Instant app launches and almost no loading times
• Smooth performance with heavy apps like Xcode, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro
• Smooth ARM system virtualization with UTM or Parallels
• Effortless multitasking with universal or native apps
🔋 Battery Life
• Up to 20 hours of moderate use
• Excellent thermal management and energy efficiency
🎮 Graphics and Editing
• 4K video editing without issues
• Limited gaming, though some run well with Rosetta 2
🧠 Neural Engine and AI
• Accelerates machine learning tasks
• Improves performance in creative apps that use artificial intelligence
🌐 Compatibility and Ecosystem
• Rosetta 2 translates x86 apps to ARM with almost no performance loss
• Excellent integration with iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, etc.
• Can run iOS/iPadOS apps
🚫 Limitations
• Reduced compatibility with specific x86 apps or older drivers
• Limited x86 virtualization (not compatible with VirtualBox or VMware)
• RAM and SSD are not upgradable after purchase
✅ Conclusion
After completing the Web Development course using a Mac with the M1 chip, I was able to finish all subjects without major issues.

The only difficulty was virtualization of operating systems, as it's not possible to run x86 environments with traditional solutions like VirtualBox or VMware. However, with UTM Virtual Machine, I was able to overcome that limitation.
Therefore, I decided to create this blog to share in-depth how to use UTM and make the most out of the Mac ecosystem for web development.

title: HOMEBREW
subtitle: Installation and use of Homebrew
description: How to get the most out of your Mac with Homebrew
content: Homebrew is a package installer for macOS
Why do I need a package installer?

I'm sorry to say this, but Apple's App Store for Mac is, let's put it this way, limited. Often, for specific programs, you may not find them or... Oh, surprise! You may only be able to install them using the Homebrew installer from the program's official page.
Can I get viruses, mess up my computer, slow it down... in short, can it be bad for my Mac?
Absolutely NO, for several reasons...
The package installer is maintained by a large community, which you can check out in the links at the end of its website.

The installer optimizes the installation, meaning it automatically installs the version that matches your Mac. If it’s an Intel chip, it installs the Intel version; if it's an Apple Silicon chip, it installs the Silicon version, also considering the operating system version you have, like Big Sur, Monterey, Ventura... This is a big advantage because it searches for the correct program and version for you, which, let’s face it, can be a hassle to find and install manually.
It installs all packages in their own directory, as explained on the main page, so the program's files aren't scattered around any directory.
Its installation and uninstallation are simple, as are the installation and uninstallation of the packages themselves.
Don’t be scared if you feel uneasy about using the terminal. It’s easier than it looks, and in the end, you’ll get the hang of it...
So, with all that said, roll up your sleeves, and let’s get to work!
<hr>
Installing Homebrew
In this video, we will explain:
- How to install Homebrew (Video Start - 4:00), run in the terminal -> /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
- How to see the available commands and help in Homebrew -> brew help

- How to search for a package by name by running in the terminal -> brew search package_name but there's another way via its searcher. My recommendation is that when you want to search or install a program (any program), search for it here first, and if you find it, install it using Homebrew.
- How to install and uninstall cask packages (Video 4:00 - 6:43), run in the terminal -> brew install --cask package_name -> example: brew install cask telegram
- How to install formulae packages, for example, in the video we’ll install Composer (Video 6:43 - 12:06), run in the terminal -> brew install package_name -> example: brew install composer
- How to see the packages you have installed by running -> brew list
- How to update Homebrew's package list -> brew update
- How to update Homebrew and the installed packages -> brew upgrade
- How to uninstall Homebrew (Video 12:06 - End) run in the terminal -> /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/uninstall.sh)"

title: UTM
subtitle: UTM, a new Virtual Machine
description: We will analyze in depth the UTM virtual machine based on QEMU
content: UTM is a Virtual Machine for macOS
What makes UTM special?

To virtualize operating systems on a Mac with an M1 chip, we can only do it with Parallels, which is paid and very expensive, with VMWare, which requires registration, with VirtualBox for ARM which is still in Beta and doesn't work well, and with QEMU, which is very complicated to use.

The UTM Virtual Machine is the graphical version of the QEMU virtual machine. QEMU is an open-source virtual machine that operates via commands, i.e., through the terminal. It’s a very complete machine for advanced users.
With UTM, it’s much easier. It’s free, and you can download it from here. The main page of UTM. If you choose to download it, you will need to update it yourself.
You can also download it through the AppStore. It’s a one-time purchase, but you’ll receive automatic updates for UTM and help the developers maintain UTM.
What can we virtualize?

With the UTM machine, we can virtualize many operating systems. ARM-based operating systems will work flawlessly, but Intel-based architectures may cause problems, so be careful. Once, during the installation of a very unusual Intel 32-bit OS, my MacBook overheated, and I had to abort the installation.
Which operating systems have I managed to virtualize?
The OSs have ranged from Windows 2.0.3, Windows XP, Windows 10 ARM, Windows 11 ARM, Ubuntu Server ARM, Kali ARM, Debian ARM, Windows Server 2008 R2,...
Is it difficult to use?

No, but if you come from VirtualBox, it might take a little longer to understand how it works. The installations are a bit more complicated, but once you learn, I think you won't want to use anything else.
Well, enough talk, let’s get to work
Installing UTM
First, download the UTM.dmg file from the main page of UTM or if you want, directly from the link here.

title: Crop 1:1 Images to 16:9 Using FFmpeg, the Great Unknown
subtitle: Easily turn your square images into professional panoramic formats
description: How to crop 1:1 square images to 16:9 format on Mac using FFmpeg, with Homebrew installation instructions in another post.
content: 🔧 What is FFmpeg?
FFmpeg is a powerful command-line tool for processing video, audio, and images. Although widely used in professional environments, it remains a hidden gem for many casual users.
Learn more on its official website: ffmpeg.org.
🛠️ Installing FFmpeg on macOS
If you don't have Homebrew installed yet, check out our guide: Installing Homebrew on Mac.
Once Homebrew is installed, installing FFmpeg is as simple as running:
brew install ffmpeg
You can verify the installation with:
ffmpeg -version
🖼️ Cropping a 1:1 square image to 16:9 format
Imagine you have a 1024x1024 pixel image (1:1 ratio) and you want to professionally crop it to a panoramic 16:9 format.
The basic command would be:
ffmpeg -i input.jpeg -vf "crop=iw:iw*9/16:0:(ih-iw*9/16)/2" output.jpeg
This command crops the image centered both horizontally and vertically.
🔼 Custom vertical adjustment
Want to move the image up or down within the crop?
To move it up by 100 pixels:
ffmpeg -i input.jpeg -vf "crop=iw:iw*9/16:0:100" output.jpeg
To move it down by 150 pixels:
ffmpeg -i input.jpeg -vf "crop=iw:iw*9/16:0:-150" output.jpeg
📏 Understanding the crop filter
The crop filter syntax is:
crop=width:height:x:y

- width: width of the crop
- height: height of the crop
- x: horizontal offset
- y: vertical offset
This lets you easily customize how your image is positioned inside the 16:9 frame.
🎯 Conclusion

With just a few commands, you can transform square images into professional panoramic crops — perfect for social media, presentations, banners, or web projects. A simple trick that will save you tons of time!

title: Transforming Audio, Video, and Images with FFmpeg
subtitle: Easily convert your audio, video, and image files using FFmpeg
alt: Transforming audio, video, and images with FFmpeg
description: Learn how to convert audio, video, and image files using FFmpeg, a powerful and versatile tool.
content: 🔧 What is FFmpeg?
FFmpeg is a powerful and versatile command-line tool for processing video, audio, and images.
More information on its official website: ffmpeg.org.
🛠️ Installing FFmpeg on macOS
If you haven't installed Homebrew yet, check out our guide: Installing Homebrew on Mac.
Once you have Homebrew, installing FFmpeg is as simple as running:
brew install ffmpeg
Verify the installation with:
ffmpeg -version
🎵 Converting Audio Formats
If you have a music CD and want to extract the tracks to listen to them on other devices, you can convert them to MP3 using the following command:
for file in *.wav; do ffmpeg -i "$file" -acodec libmp3lame -ab 192k "${file%.wav}.mp3"; done
If you have a WAV audio file and want to convert it to MP3, you can use:
ffmpeg -i input.wav -acodec libmp3lame -ab 192k output.mp3
This will convert the WAV file to MP3 with a bitrate of 192 kbps.
🎥 Converting Video Formats
If you have a video in AVI format and want to convert it to MP4, use:
ffmpeg -i input.avi -c:v libx264 -c:a aac output.mp4
This will convert the AVI file to MP4 using the H.264 video codec and AAC audio codec.
To change the resolution of the video, for example to 1280x720, add the parameter:
ffmpeg -i input.avi -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -s 1280x720 output.mp4
🖼️ Converting Image Formats
If you have an image in PNG format and want to convert it to JPEG, use:
ffmpeg -i input.png -q:v 2 output.jpg
This converts the PNG file to JPEG with a visual quality level of 2 (where 1 is best and 31 is worst).
To resize the image, for example to 800x600 pixels, add the -s parameter:
ffmpeg -i input.png -q:v 2 -s 800x600 output.jpg
This resizes the image to 800x600 pixels and converts it to JPEG.
🎯 Conclusion

FFmpeg is an incredibly versatile tool that allows you to convert audio, video, and image files easily and efficiently. With just a few commands, you can change formats, adjust resolutions, and control quality.

Whether you're extracting tracks from a CD, converting videos to more common formats, or resizing images, FFmpeg has the tools to get the job done. Explore its capabilities and enhance your multimedia workflow!
💡 Bonus Tip:

If you don't remember the exact commands or want to explore additional options, you can use an AI tool like ChatGPT to help you generate, adjust, or customize commands based on your needs. Just describe what you want to do and get a fast solution!
You can also install FFmpeg on Windows 11 using the winget package manager. Just run the following command in the terminal (open CMD as administrator):
winget install ffmpeg

title: yt-dlp
subtitle: Download YouTube and other platform videos from the terminal using yt-dlp
alt: Video downloading with yt-dlp from the terminal
description: Learn how to download videos, playlists, or audio from YouTube and many other platforms using yt-dlp — a modern, powerful command-line tool.
content: 📦 What is yt-dlp?
yt-dlp is a command-line tool that lets you download videos, audio, or playlists from YouTube and many other platforms. It’s an improved and actively maintained fork of youtube-dl.
More info and documentation available on its official GitHub repo: github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp.
🛠️ Installing yt-dlp on macOS
If you have Homebrew installed, you can easily add yt-dlp by running:
brew install yt-dlp
Verify the installation with:
yt-dlp --version
This will show the installed version number, confirming everything’s ready to go.
🪟 Installation on Windows
On Windows 11, you can use the winget package manager to install it:
winget install yt-dlp
You can also download the executable directly from its GitHub releases page if you prefer using it without installation.
▶️ Downloading a YouTube video
To download a video in the best available quality, simply run:
yt-dlp "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XXXXXXXXXXX"
This will download the video using the best possible combination of video and audio quality.
🎧 Downloading only the audio (e.g., in MP3 format)
If you only want the audio from a video, use the --extract-audio flag and specify the format with --audio-format:
yt-dlp -x --audio-format mp3 "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XXXXXXXXXXX"
This will extract the audio and convert it to MP3 automatically using FFmpeg (if installed).
📜 Downloading a playlist
Want to download all videos from a playlist? Just pass the full playlist link:
yt-dlp "https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=XXXXXXXXXXX"
yt-dlp will grab every video from the playlist, keeping the titles and original order.
🎛️ Customizing file names
You can define the output name format using the -o option. For example:
yt-dlp -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XXXXXXXXXXX"
This will save the file using the video’s title and its original extension.
💾 Downloading subtitles
If you want to grab subtitles too, add the --write-subs flag. To download them in English, use:
yt-dlp --write-subs --sub-lang en "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XXXXXXXXXXX"
If you also want to embed the subtitles directly into the video file, add --embed-subs.
💡 Pro tip:
You can combine yt-dlp with FFmpeg to convert, merge, or trim downloaded files. For instance, download audio as WAV and then convert to MP3, or resize a video after downloading it.
🎯 Conclusion

yt-dlp is an incredibly useful and flexible tool for downloading multimedia content from multiple platforms. Whether you want to save videos for offline viewing, extract audio for your playlists, or automate your downloads, yt-dlp does it all right from the terminal.
With a single line of code, you can control quality, format, subtitles, and more. Explore its options and make your multimedia workflow even more powerful!
💬 Bonus tip:

If you can’t remember the exact commands, ask an AI like ChatGPT to generate them for you — just say something like “I want to download the audio from this video as MP3,” and you’ll get the exact line ready to paste into your terminal.
Always remember to respect the platform’s terms of service and copyright laws when downloading content.

title: Retro Virtual Machine
subtitle: Emulate classic computers like the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC with Retro Virtual Machine
alt: Retro Virtual Machine emulator interface showing a ZX Spectrum
description: Discover Retro Virtual Machine — a modern, cross-platform emulator that brings classic computers like the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC back to life with authentic and elegant accuracy.
content: 🕹️ What is Retro Virtual Machine?

Retro Virtual Machine (RVM) is a classic computer emulator carefully designed to offer a realistic yet modern experience. It emulates systems such as the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC, faithfully reproducing both their hardware and their visual and sound behavior.
What makes it stand out is its interface: clean, fluid, and full of subtle details that take you straight back to the 80s — but with all the conveniences of the 21st century.
You can learn more or download it from its official website: retrovirtualmachine.org.
🧩 Key features
• Compatibility with ZX Spectrum (16K, 48K, 128K, +2A, +3) and Amstrad CPC (464, 6128).
• Modern interface with floating windows and 3D views of the machines.
• Support for tapes, disks, snapshots, and instant loading.
• Record video and audio directly from the emulator.
• Session synchronization for machine states and settings.
• Accurate emulation of original sound, color, and timing.
💻 Installation on macOS
The easiest way to install Retro Virtual Machine on macOS is by downloading the package from its official website:
https://www.retrovirtualmachine.org/download
Simply open the .dmg file and drag the app into your Applications folder. Ready to go!
Another way to install Retro Virtual Machine on macOS is by using Homebrew. Just run the following command in the terminal:
brew install --cask retro-virtual-machine
This will automatically download and install the latest available version of RVM on your system.
🪟 Installation on Windows
On Windows, just download the installer from the same page and follow the setup steps:
RetroVirtualMachineSetup.exe
The program is fully portable, so you can also run it without installation if you prefer.
🎮 Loading a tape or a game
Once RVM is open, you can drag and drop a tape file (.tzx or .tap) or disk file (.dsk) directly onto the emulator window. It will automatically detect the machine type and begin loading.
You can also use the top menu to switch models or insert virtual media.
📼 Saving and restoring game states
Retro Virtual Machine lets you save the exact state of the system at any time. Just press CMD + S (on Mac) or Ctrl + S (on Windows) to create a snapshot, and load it later with CMD + O or Ctrl + O.
This is perfect for tough games or continuing your BASIC programming experiments exactly where you left off.
🔊 Recording audio and video
Want to share your gameplay or tutorials? RVM can record both audio and video directly. Simply enable recording from the top menu and export your results as MP4 or WAV files.
🧠 Developer mode
If you enjoy programming in assembly or creating retro demos, RVM includes powerful debugging tools — memory inspection, breakpoints, and real-time Z80 control. Perfect for retro scene developers!
🎯 Conclusion
Retro Virtual Machine isn’t just an emulator — it’s a nostalgic experience, thoughtfully crafted for those who grew up with 8-bit computers or anyone curious about that golden age of computing.
Its blend of technical precision, modern interface, and ease of use makes it one of the best ways to enjoy the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC on your current computer.
💡 Final tip:

If you’d like to try classic games or explore historical software, visit sites like World of Spectrum, CPC Rulez, or Internet Archive, where you’ll find thousands of titles ready to download and use with RVM.

title: The Emulation Station
subtitle: Play retro classics directly in your browser thanks to Internet Archive
alt: The Emulation Station interface on Internet Archive showing retro games in the browser
description: Discover The Emulation Station by Internet Archive, a collection that lets you play thousands of classic console and PC games directly in your browser, with no installation required.
content: 🕹️ What is The Emulation Station?

The Emulation Station is an amazing collection within Internet Archive that allows you to play classic video games directly in your browser, without needing to install emulators or download additional files.
Thanks to modern technologies like JavaScript-based emulation, you can relive historic titles from multiple platforms with just a click.
You can explore the collection here: The Emulation Station on Internet Archive.
🎮 What kind of games can you find?
The collection is massive and spans multiple systems and eras:
• Games from classic consoles like NES, SNES, Sega Genesis, and PlayStation.
• Titles from old computers such as MS-DOS, Windows 3.x, and Windows 95.
• Historical software and interactive applications.
• Arcade and coin-op games.
• Educational and shareware titles from the 80s and 90s.
All of this accessible without leaving your browser.
⚙️ How does it work?
When you open a game, Internet Archive automatically loads an emulator in the background (based on projects like DOSBox or MAME adapted for the web).
The system emulates the original hardware, allowing you to interact as if you were using the real machine.
Additionally, many titles come pre-configured, avoiding technical complications.
🖥️ Browser experience
One of the biggest advantages is convenience:
• No installation required.
• Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
• Compatible with most modern browsers.
• Allows gameplay even on low-end devices.
However, performance may vary depending on your system and browser.
⌨️ Controls and configuration
Games are usually mapped automatically to the keyboard, although many allow custom control configurations or the use of compatible controllers.
For older PC games, you can interact with keyboard and mouse just like on the original system.
💾 Saving your progress
Some emulators allow you to save your game state directly in the browser using local storage.
This means you can continue your progress later, although not all games support this feature.
📚 Digital preservation
Beyond entertainment, The Emulation Station has enormous historical value. Internet Archive works to preserve software that might otherwise be lost over time.
This includes games, operating systems, and applications that defined an era in computing and digital entertainment.
⚠️ Limitations
Although it’s a fantastic tool, it does have some limitations:
• Some games may have performance issues.
• Not all titles are complete or perfectly configured.
• The experience is not always 100% faithful to the original hardware.
Still, for a quick and accessible experience, it’s more than enough.
🎯 Conclusion
The Emulation Station is a direct gateway to the past of video games and computing, accessible to anyone with a browser.
Whether for nostalgia or curiosity, it offers a simple and legal way to explore thousands of classic titles without technical hassle.
Perfect for both veteran players and new generations who want to discover how it all began.
Hope you enjoy it!
💡 Final tip:

Try different systems and games, especially MS-DOS or classic Windows titles, where you’ll find true hidden gems. And if you're looking for a more advanced experience, you can always combine this with local emulators like Retro Virtual Machine.
